Acilia Sud — Rome, Italy

🟡 Local-source safety assessment · 155 areas reviewed individually Methodology →

Reviewed — no findings area reviewed, nothing documented — not a safety rating

In detail

Acilia Sud, the southern half of this residential district near the Ostia Antica/Malafede boundary, is an ordinary area of apartment blocks, local shops and small businesses. No specific documented crime incidents, red-zone designations, or recurring press coverage of assaults or drug dealing were found for this area in the research conducted for this listing. A calm, default rating applies for both day and night in the absence of documented concerns.

This area was reviewed as part of a structured local-source assessment — the same area-level review applied to every neighbourhood in Rome, drawing on local and national news, municipal and police-published material and official surveys where they exist. The review reached nothing traveller-relevant for this area, so it carries no rating. That is deliberate: an absence of reporting is not evidence that an area is safe, and Wandroz does not convert one into the other.

Frequently asked questions

Is Acilia Sud safe?

Acilia Sud was reviewed at area level and no traveller-relevant safety concern was documented for it in the sources checked. Wandroz records that as no findings, not as a safety rating: an absence of reporting is not evidence that an area is safe. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Rome publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Why does Acilia Sud have no rating?

Because the review found nothing to rate it on. Areas with documented, sourced signals get a level; areas without them are shown as reviewed with no findings, so you can tell the difference between an area that was checked and came back clear of documented issues and one that was never looked at. Both are treated as inconclusive here rather than as reassurance.

Is Acilia Sud a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Nothing documented argues against it, and nothing documented argues for it either. For a stay, weigh it against the rated areas on the Rome map and check recent reviews for the specific street. You can search accommodation already scoped to this area using the Booking.com link on this page.
